OPUS RECHECK OVERRIDE (was 'ά'). OVERRIDE. Pixel-dumped the mark (strip-01, y190-201, x89-96). It starts as a horizontal bar, descends to the RIGHT, then curls back LEFT at the bottom rows. That is the smooth-breathing/apostrophe hook. The acute in this font (e.g. over the ο of ’νόματος on the very next line, and over the ε of προστιθέασιν) is a monotonic straight diagonal of constant width with no leftward curl. Placed side by side at 14x, the disputed mark is indistinguishable from the breathing of ἀεὶ on the line above and from the aphaeresis apostrophe of ’νόματος on the line below, and plainly unlike either acute. Sonnet's stated ground is also wrong on its own terms: the line-3 descender IS visible, as a separate thin stroke at y178-186, x81-84 — well above and left of the hook, which sits below line 3's baseline and directly over the α's right shoulder. The reading is semantically odd (Bonitz's book sigla are otherwise bare: Ρα, Ρβ, Πγ, Ζγδ), but it is odd under 'ά' too, and this is a diplomatic transcription: the ink shows a breathing-shaped hook.
